problem:
The center of the hyperbola $4{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-8x+6y=11$ is$\,\,($
{{field-1}}$,$
{{field-2}}
$).$
worked_solution:
The equation of a horizontal hyperbola centered at $(h,k)$ is given by

$$
\frac{(x-h)^{2}}{{a}^{2}}-\frac{(y-k)^{2}}{{b}^{2}}=1.
$$

To rewrite the given equation in standard form, group the $x$ and $y$ terms and complete the squares:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{x}^{2}-{y}^{2}-8x+6y & =11 \\ 4({x}^{2}-2x)-({y}^{2}-6y) & =11 \\ 4[(x-1)^{2}-1]-[(y-3)^{2}-9] & =11 \\ 4(x-1)^{2}-4-(y-3)^{2}+9 & =11 \\ 4(x-1)^{2}-(y-3)^{2} & =11+4-9 \\ 4(x-1)^{2}-(y-3)^{2} & =6 \\ \frac{(x-1)^{2}}{3/2}-\frac{(y-3)^{2}}{6} & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, the center of the hyperbola is $(\,1,3\,).$
